idx_lede:
An open-source rhythm game that runs right in your browser.
There's nothing to install. At all.

idx_stage1_body: The cursor follows your mouse. It is the thing that reaches a note, and it is the thing a bullet hits, so both jobs are the same hand.
idx_stage1_alt: The playfield: the cursor, and a note arriving beside it.
idx_stage2_body: Bullets close in from every direction. Taking one does not break the note you are on — hits are counted on their own line, beside the judgments.
idx_stage2_alt: The playfield with bullets closing in from every side of the cursor.
idx_stage3_body: Hold the cursor on the note and press on the beat. Perfect, Great, Good, Bad, Miss — how close you were is what you score. A long note is held to its end.
idx_stage3_alt: A note judged Perfect as the cursor lands on it.
idx_stage4_body: Every note you land carries the combo on. Drop none of them and it is a Full Combo; land all of them Perfect and it is All Perfect. Accuracy and the rank come out of the same count.
idx_stage4_alt: The result screen: score, max combo, accuracy and the judgment counts.
idx_spec_browser_v: Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Opera. Safari and phones are not supported.
idx_spec_input_v: Mouse and keyboard together — the cursor dodges, the keys hit.
idx_spec_account_v: Google sign-in, and a nickname you pick once on the way in.
idx_spec_price_v: Free, all of it. URLATE LITE stays a non-commercial game, for good.
idx_spec_license_v: Code under AGPL-3.0, game assets under CC BY-NC-ND 4.0.

info_game_title: What kind of game is URLATE?
info_game_p1: URLATE is an open-source rhythm game built with web technologies.
info_game_p2: You must move the cursor to dodge bullets flying from all directions while hitting notes at the precise timing.
info_game_p3: A rhythm game project that started under the name MyRhy in 2017 has evolved into its current form after many versions of experimentation.
info_lite_p1: URLATE is a game developed since 2018, with its first demo released in 2020, and crowdfunded through Tumblbug.
info_lite_p2: After funding, two rounds of CBT incorporated user feedback, and the game officially launched on November 11, 2021.
info_lite_p3: Afterwards, efforts were made to improve the business model, refine operations, and strengthen the team, but due to various difficulties, the sustainability of the game could not be secured. As a result, the service was ultimately shut down in January 2022.
info_lite_p4: URLATE LITE is a project to develop and distribute an open-source game based on the shut-down game URLATE.
info_lite_p5: All monetization elements from the original URLATE — such as the store and memberships — have been removed, leaving only the gameplay and editor features.
info_source_title: Where can I find the source code for URLATE?
info_source_p1: You can view the original source code at the links above. For information on usage and modification, please refer to the README in the repository.

info_news_p1: Updates on the game's development and behind-the-scenes can be found on Coupy's
info_upkeep_p1: URLATE LITE plans to continuously improve its shortcomings through regular updates.
info_upkeep_p2: URLATE NEXT is currently in planning, which will re-optimize the URLATE client and add new features.
info_upkeep_p3: Contributions via browser extensions for new features or PRs/Issues through the GitHub repository are always welcome — your interest is appreciated!
